label: How To Use The Guides Library
description: Get the most out of dima's Guides Library with tips on searching, navigating, and quickly finding exactly what you need.
content: How to Use The Guides Library Our Guides Library is designed to help you find answers and guidance whenever you need it on the platform. We’ve made it easy for you to access guides wherever you are: The Full Guides Library: Click the "Guides" icon in the main sidebar to explore the complete guides collection. Quick Search Dialog: Hit the ? (question mark) icon in the top right corner of the app to instantly search the Guides Library. When you select a search result, it will open in a new tab so you don’t lose your progress or place in the app. Choose How You Want to Learn Everyone learns differently, and our Guides Library is designed to fit your preferred style: Prefer Watching? Each guide includes a short video created by the dima team, showing you exactly how to use the feature. Like to Read? Detailed step by step written instructions follow the video, including explanations for why things work a certain way. Just Have a Quick Question? Skip directly to asking our dima chatbot. Get fast, personalized answers without needing to watch or read the entire guide. Need More Assistance? The Guides Library covers a lot, but every brand has unique workflows. If you’ve used a guide and still need help, our team is here for you. Reach out to your account manager for tailored support whenever you need it.

label: Users
description: Learn how to add, edit, and delete users to manage workspace access and permissions.
content: Managing Users The Users screen is where you can manage who has access to your workspace (such as your "Made for You" dashboards) and control their permissions. By assigning specific roles, you ensure the right team members have the appropriate level of access, whether they just need to view data or actively edit content. You can manage all workspace users directly from the Manage page. 1. Accessing the Users Menu All user management takes place in one central location: 1. Navigate to the main sidebar and click the Manage icon. 2. Select the Users tab located in the secondary menu. 2. Adding a User 1. From the Users tab, click the Add User button in the top right corner of the page. 2. You will be prompted to select a User Role for the new team member. The role you choose dictates their permissions and the information you need to fill out: Viewer Viewers can only view shared dashboards and their content. Username: A unique identifier used for logging in. Display Name: The name visible within the workspace. Contact Email: The email address associated with the user. Password & Confirm Password: Create a secure login password. Timezone: Select the user's local time zone from the dropdown menu. Editor Editors can view and edit content, but only for the specific companies you assign to them. Assigned Companies: Choose the specific companies this user is allowed to edit. Username: A unique identifier used for logging in. Display Name: The name visible within the workspace. Password & Confirm Password: Create a secure login password. Timezone: Select the user's local time zone from the dropdown menu. 3. Click the Add User button at the bottom right corner of the form to create the profile and grant them access. 3. Editing a User If you need to update a user's details or adjust an editor's assigned companies: 1. Locate the specific user card you want to update in your list. 2. Click the vertical three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of that specific card. 3. Select Edit User from the dropdown menu. 4. Update the available fields depending on their assigned role. Important Restrictions: You cannot edit or change a user's Username once their profile has been created. You cannot change a user's role (e.g., switching a Viewer to an Editor). If a team member needs a different role, you must delete their current profile and create a new one. 5. Click Update User in the bottom right corner to save your changes. 4. Deleting a User Warning: Deleting a user will immediately revoke their access to your workspace. If they are a Viewer, they will lose all ability to see shared dashboards. 1. Locate the specific user card you want to remove. 2. Click the three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of the card. 3. Select Delete User from the dropdown menu. 4. A confirmation pop up will appear to ensure you want to proceed. Click the Delete button at the bottom right to finalize the removal.

label: Topics
description: Learn how to add, edit, and delete custom topics to categorize incoming posts for your brand.
content: Managing Topics A Topic is a custom category used to classify incoming posts about your company. For example, you might create topics for "Customer Service," "Marketing Campaigns," or "Product Reviews." Topics allow you to easily filter relevant posts and build targeted reports. You can manage all your custom categories directly from the Manage page. Accessing the Topics Menu All topic management happens in one central location: 1. Navigate to the main sidebar and click the Manage icon. 2. Select the Topics tab located in the secondary menu. 3. Choose the company where you want to manage its topics. Adding a Topic 1. From the Topics tab, click the Add Topic button in the top right corner of the page. 2. A form will appear. Fill in the required fields: Name: The title of your category (e.g., "Corporate News"). Description: A brief explanation of what this topic covers. This helps dima accurately classify incoming posts. 3. Click the Add Topic button at the bottom right corner of the form to save your new category. Editing a Topic If you need to tweak the name or description of an existing category: 1. Locate the specific topic card you want to update in your list. 2. Click the vertical three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of that specific card. 3. Select Edit Topic from the dropdown menu. 4. Update the Name or Description fields as needed. 5. Click Update Topic in the bottom right corner to save your changes. Deleting a Topic Warning: Deleting a topic cannot be undone. If you delete a topic, it will be permanently removed, and any historical posts previously classified under this topic will instantly lose that label. 1. Locate the specific topic card you want to remove. 2. Click the three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of the card. 3. Select Delete Topic from the dropdown. 4. A confirmation pop up will appear to ensure you want to proceed. Click the Delete button at the bottom right of the pop up to finalize the removal.

label: Restoring Posts
description: Learn how to recover previously deleted posts and bring them back into your monitoring feeds.
content: Restoring Posts As you curate your data, you might delete a post only to realize later that it is actually relevant to your brand. dima keeps a secure archive of your removed content, allowing you to easily recover and restore any deleted posts. 1. Selecting Deleted Posts To recover deleted posts, first navigate to the main sidebar and click on the Manage icon. Then, select the Deleted Posts tab in the secondary menu. You will now see a feed of all previously removed content for that company, just like in the screenshot above. Select Individual Posts: Click the small checkbox in the top left corner of each post card to select specific posts you want to recover. Select All Posts: To recover every post on the current page, click the main checkbox at the top left of the feed, next to the Restore Posts icon. 2. Finalizing the Restoration 1. After selecting your desired posts, click the Restore Posts icon (located just below the search bar at the top left of the screen). 2. A confirmation pop up will appear. 3. Click the Restore button in the bottom right corner of the pop up to immediately send the posts back to your active monitoring feeds.

label: Own Pages
description: Learn how to add, edit, and delete your company's official social media pages for dedicated tracking and analysis.
content: Managing Own Pages Own Pages are the official social media profiles or groups owned and managed by your company. By connecting them to dima, you unlock a dedicated analytics module to track every post you publish, analyze performance metrics (like engagement and views), determine your best times to post, and evaluate your content strategy. You can manage all your connected profiles directly from the Manage page. Accessing the Own Pages Menu All management actions for your official pages take place in one central location: 1. Navigate to the main sidebar and click the Manage icon. 2. Select the specific Company you want to manage from the list. Use the search bar at the top to quickly find it if you have multiple brands. 3. Ensure you are on the Own Pages tab. Adding an Own Page 1. From the Own Pages tab, click the button Add Own Page button located at the top right. 2. A form will appear. Fill in the required basic information: Name: The internal name you want to use for this page. Platform: Select the social media network (e.g., Facebook, Instagram, X). URL: Paste the direct link to the page or profile. 3. Tracking Preferences: By default, dima tracks everything via the "Track all posts on this page?" checkbox. If you only want to track specific types of posts, uncheck this box. A new Comment textbox will appear. Use this box to describe exactly what types of posts dima should track (e.g., "Only track posts about our summer campaign"). 4. Click the Add Own Page button at the bottom right corner of the form to save the profile. Editing an Own Page If a URL changes or you need to adjust your tracking preferences: 1. Locate the specific Own Page card you want to update. 2. Click the vertical three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of that specific card. 3. Select Edit Own Page from the dropdown menu. 4. Update the Name, Platform, URL, or tracking checkboxes as needed. 5. Click Update Own Page in the bottom right corner to save your changes. Deleting an Own Page Warning: Deleting an Own Page will completely remove it from the company's tracked pages and halt all active monitoring for that specific profile. 1. Locate the specific Own Page card you want to remove. 2. Click the three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of the card. 3. Select Delete Own Page from the dropdown menu. 4. A secondary prompt will appear. Click Delete Own Page again. 5. A final confirmation pop up will appear to ensure you want to proceed. Click the Delete button at the bottom right to finalize the removal.

label: Locations
description: Learn how to add, edit, and delete physical company locations to track Google Reviews.
content: Managing Locations A Location in dima represents a physical company branch linked to a Google Maps place. By adding a location, dima will automatically fetch and monitor all Google Reviews for that specific branch. You can manage all your connected physical locations directly from the Manage page. Accessing the Locations Menu All management actions for your physical branches take place in one central location: 1. Navigate to the main sidebar and click the Manage icon (the settings gear icon). 2. Select the specific Company you want to manage from the list. You can use the search bar at the top to quickly find it. 3. Click on the Locations tab in the secondary menu. Adding a Location 1. From the Locations tab, click the Add Location button in the top right corner of the screen. 2. A form will appear. Fill in the required fields: Name: Type in the internal name of the location (e.g., "Downtown Branch"). URL: Paste the direct Google Maps URL for this specific physical place. 3. Click the Add Location button at the bottom right corner of the form. dima will now begin fetching Google Reviews for this spot. Editing a Location If a location's details or Google Maps link changes: 1. Locate the specific location card you want to update. 2. Click the vertical three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of that specific card. 3. Select Edit Company Location from the dropdown menu. 4. Update the Name or URL fields as needed. 5. Click Update Company Location in the bottom right corner to save your changes. Deleting a Location Warning: Deleting a location will remove it from your tracked locations list, and dima will stop fetching new reviews for that branch. 1. Locate the specific location card you want to remove. 2. Click the three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of the card. 3. Select Delete Company Location from the dropdown menu. 4. A confirmation pop up will appear to ensure you want to proceed. Click the Delete button at the bottom right to finalize the removal.

label: Groups
description: Learn how to add, edit, and delete Facebook Groups to monitor community discussions and trends.
content: Managing Groups In dima, a Group specifically refers to a public Facebook Group. Since Facebook Groups act as open social communities centered around specific themes, locations, or interests, tracking them allows you to monitor what users are actively discussing within these dedicated communities. You can manage the specific groups you want to track directly from the Manage page. Accessing the Groups Menu All management actions for your tracked Facebook Groups take place here: 1. Navigate to the main sidebar and click the Manage icon. 2. Select the specific Company you want to manage from your list. 3. Click the Groups tab in the secondary menu. Adding a Group 1. From the Groups tab, click the Add Group button in the top right corner of the page. 2. A form will appear. Fill in the required basic information: Name: An internal name to identify the group. URL: Paste the direct link to the public Facebook Group. 3. Tracking Preferences: By default, dima tracks everything via the "Track all posts in this group?" checkbox. If you only want to track specific types of posts, uncheck this box. A Comment textbox will appear. Use this box to describe exactly what types of posts dima should track from this community (e.g., "Only fetch posts that mention our brand"). 4. Click the Add Group button at the bottom right corner of the form to save it and begin monitoring. Editing a Group If you need to update a URL or adjust your tracking preferences: 1. Locate the specific group card you want to update in your list. 2. Click the three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of that specific card. 3. Select Edit Group from the dropdown menu. 4. Update the Name, URL, or tracking checkboxes as needed. 5. Click Update Group in the bottom right corner to save your changes. Deleting a Group Warning: Deleting a group will completely remove it from your tracking list, and dima will stop fetching new community discussions from that URL. 1. Locate the specific group card you want to remove. 2. Click the three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of the card. 3. Select Delete Group from the dropdown menu. 4. A confirmation pop up will appear to ensure you want to proceed. Click the Delete button at the bottom right to finalize the removal.

label: Contacts
description: Learn how to add, edit, and delete contacts to receive important reports and notifications.
content: Managing Contacts A Contact is a designated email address and mobile phone number where you want to receive reports and alerts from dima. You can assign multiple contacts to different companies to ensure the right team members always receive scheduled reports and updates. You can manage your notification roster directly from the Manage page. Accessing the Contacts Menu All contact management for a specific brand happens in one central location: 1. Navigate to the main sidebar and click the Manage icon. 2. Select the specific Company you want to manage from your connected brands list. 3. Click the Contacts tab located in the secondary menu. Adding a Contact 1. From the Contacts tab, click the Add Contact button in the top right corner of the page. 2. A form will appear. Fill in the required fields: Name: The full name of the team member or stakeholder. Email: The address where reports and updates should be sent. Phone Number: The mobile number for the contact. 3. Click the Add Contact button at the bottom right corner of the form to save the new team member to your list. Editing a Contact If a team member's email or phone number changes: 1. Locate the specific contact card you want to update. 2. Click the three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of that specific card. 3. Select Edit Contact from the dropdown menu. 4. Update the Name, Email, or Phone Number fields as needed. 5. Click Update Contact in the bottom right corner to save your changes. A success message will appear at the bottom right of the screen confirming the update. Deleting a Contact If someone leaves the team or no longer needs to receive scheduled reports, you can safely remove them: 1. Locate the specific contact card you want to remove. 2. Click the three dot menu ( ⋮ ) in the top right corner of the card. 3. Select Delete Contact (written in red) from the dropdown menu. 4. A confirmation pop up will appear to ensure you want to proceed. Click the Delete button at the bottom right of the pop up to permanently remove the contact.

label: Creating Dashboards
description: Learn how to build, edit, customize, filter, share, and manage custom dashboards in the Made For You module.
content: Managing Dashboards When you navigate to the Made For You module, you will land on the main screen where all of your created dashboards are housed. If your workspace is empty, you can build your first dashboard to get started or choose from pre designed templates. 1. Creating a New Dashboard 1. From the main Made For You screen, click the Click to Add button to begin building your new dashboard. 2. Fill in the initial setup form: Dashboard Name: Enter a clear title for this workspace. Background Accent Color (Optional): Choose a custom background color to personalize the workspace. Assigned Companies: Select the specific brands or companies you want to track within this dashboard. Company Accent Colors (Optional): Assign specific accent colors to selected companies to distinguish them across your data visuals. 3. Choose your dashboard starting point: Start from Scratch: Create an empty workspace where you build and configure custom charts manually. Start from Template: Choose from pre configured layouts such as Organic Content & UGC , Own Page Statistics , and other specialized templates to auto populate your workspace. Once configured, save your settings to enter your new dashboard. 2. Managing & Positioning Charts Inside your dashboard workspace, you can fully organize and control your layout: Drag & Reposition Click and hold any chart header to drag and move it anywhere within the grid layout. Resize Charts Click and drag the edges or corners of a chart card to adjust its width and height. Refresh Data Click the Refresh button at the top of the dashboard to fetch the latest incoming data on demand. Note: Dashboards automatically fetch fresh data upon opening, but manually refreshing is useful if you leave the dashboard open for extended sessions. Saving Your Layout After making layout updates, moving charts, or adjusting date settings, you must click Save Dashboard to preserve your changes. If you attempt to navigate away with unsaved modifications, a prompt will ask whether you want to save or discard your changes before leaving. To learn how to build individual data visuals, visit our guide on Creating Charts . 3. Dashboard Wide Filters & Date Locking You can apply global filters across your entire dashboard to narrow down the displayed dataset without editing individual charts: Global Company & Source Filters: Use the top filter bar to include or exclude specific assigned companies or filter by data sources. Note: For an overview of the available filters and settings for each data source, see our filter guides: Audience Intelligence E Commerce Reviews Locations Conversation Analysis Date Filter: Define the exact timeframe for all data pulled across the dashboard. Locking Date Ranges: By default, dynamic date ranges move forward by one day each morning (e.g., a 7 day range of Aug 17–Aug 24 today becomes Aug 18–Aug 25 tomorrow) . Click the Lock icon next to the date selector to freeze the start and end dates permanently whenever you access this dashboard. Note: After locking or adjusting your date range, make sure to click Save Dashboard at the top of the screen to lock that range permanently. 4. Exporting & Sharing Exporting Options Download Full Dashboard: Export your entire dashboard layout as an image file. You can choose whether to render Data Label Values directly on the visuals or export clean Visuals Only graphics. Download Individual Charts: Hover over the vertical three dot menu ( ⋮ ) on any specific chart card, then select Download Chart to save it as an image or Download CSV to export raw data points. Sharing & Permissions Click the Share button at the top of your dashboard to collaborate with others: Invite Workspace Users: Search and select existing team members within your account to grant them dashboard access. If you don't see a specific teammate listed, refer to our guide on Adding Users to add them to your account first. Shareable Link: Generate a direct URL link to send to any verified user within your workspace. 5. Editing, Duplicating & Deleting On the main Made For You landing page, locate any dashboard card and click its vertical three dot menu ( ⋮ ) to access management options: Edit: Rename the dashboard, update assigned companies, or reassign accent colors. Duplicate: Create an instant clone of an existing dashboard, preserving all selected companies, color themes, and pre built charts. Delete: Permanently remove the dashboard and all charts housed inside it. Warning: Deleting a dashboard is permanent and cannot be undone.

label: Creating Charts
description: Learn how to build and customize charts to visualize data within your dashboards.
content: Creating Charts After creating a dashboard, you can start adding charts to visualize your data exactly how you want. By customizing data sources, chart types, and specific filters, you can build a highly tailored view of your brand's performance. 1. Initiating Chart Creation To build a new chart inside your dashboard: 1. Click the + Create button located in the top right corner, just below the dashboard's name. 2. Alternatively , if this is your first time creating a chart in an empty dashboard, you can simply click the large Create chart button located directly in the middle of the screen. 2. Selecting a Data Source Upon clicking create, you will be prompted to select the data source your chart will pull from. You can select from the following data sources when creating a chart: Audience Intelligence Locations E commerce Reviews Conversation Analysis Choose the source that best matches the data you want to visualize. 3. Customizing Your Chart After picking your data source, you will be taken to the chart builder form. Configure the following sections to shape how your data is displayed: Chart Type: Choose how you want to visualize the data. Currently supported types include Bar, Stacked Bar, Line, Area, Combo, Table, Pie, Scorecard, Insights (where you can ask a question and dima responds with an answer), and Word Cloud. Metadata: Enter a clear Title for your chart and provide a brief Description (optional) for extra context. Date Range: Select the timeframe for the data. You can set it to default to the dashboard's main date range, pick fixed custom dates, or choose a rolling window (e.g., last 30 days). Value Display: Decide how data labels are shown on the chart. Choose to display numbers, percentages, both, or none at all. Fields: Select your X axis and your Y axis (also labeled as Metric). Depending on your X axis selection, a Group By field may dynamically appear, allowing you to further categorize your data. Maximum Number of Rows: Define a row limit to prevent your chart from becoming visually cluttered. If you limit the rows, you can opt to show the excess excluded data grouped together under an "Other" category. Filters: Apply specific rules to include or exclude data based on existing filters within dima. You can filter by: Assigned Companies (from your dashboard setup) Sentiment & Emotion Platform & Post Types Topics & Labels Language, Country, & Gender 4. Finalizing Your Chart Once you are satisfied with your configurations, click the Add Chart button at the bottom right corner of the form. Your newly created chart will be instantly added to your dashboard!

label: Monitoring Locations
description: Learn how to track and filter Google Reviews for your company's physical locations.
content: Monitoring Locations dima automatically extracts and tracks Google Reviews for all the physical company locations you have connected to your account. This allows you to monitor customer feedback and location performance directly from the platform. 1. Navigating the Monitor Page The Locations module is split into two main sections: Monitor and Analysis , which can be accessed via the tabs under the top search bar. Search for a Location: Use the search bar at the top of the page (under the dima logo) to look up a specific company location. View All Locations: The Monitor page displays all of your company's connected locations alongside their overall star ratings. Read Recent Reviews: Click on any specific location card to open its detailed view. This section displays the "Recent Reviews" from different users. Review Details: Each individual review includes the user's name, the date it was posted, the text of the review, and the star rating given. Quick Filter: You can click directly on the star icons in the summary to quickly filter and see only the users who left that specific rating. 2. Using Advanced Filters For more granular control over what you are viewing, you can use the dedicated Filters menu. 1. Click the Filters button located at the top right corner of the page. 2. Filtering Range (Stars): Use the drag handles on the left and right of this slider to set the minimum and maximum star ratings you want to see. 3. Number of Reviews: Use this slider to narrow down your search to locations that have a specific volume of reviews. 4. Locations List: Scroll to the bottom of the filter page to see a list of all locations associated with the company. You can select one or multiple specific locations to focus on. 5. Click the Apply Filters button at the bottom right of the page to execute your search and update your feed.

label: Locations Analytics
description: Learn how to analyze aggregate Google Review data across all your company's physical locations.
content: Locations Analytics The Locations module includes a dedicated Analytics page that gathers customer reviews from all your connected company branches and visualizes them into easy to read charts and metrics. 1. Accessing the Dashboard & Top Level Stats To view detailed review analysis, click on the Analytics tab located at the top of the Locations module (next to the Monitor tab). At the very top of this page, you will see a quick summary of your overall performance, including: Total Locations: The number of physical branches currently tracked for this company. Total Reviews: The overall volume of reviews collected across all branches. Average Reviews: The average number of reviews received per location. 2. Breakdown by Location These bar charts help you compare the volume and quality of reviews between your different physical branches side by side. Reviews per Location: A straightforward bar chart showing the total volume of reviews for each branch. The X axis represents your individual locations, and the Y axis represents the total review count. Rating Distribution per Location: This chart uses the same layout, but each bar is split into color coded segments representing specific star ratings (Green 5 stars, Light Green 4 stars, Yellow 3 stars, Orange 2 stars, Red 1 star). This allows you to quickly spot which branches are excelling and which are receiving poor feedback. 3. Average Rating Over Time This area chart tracks how your average star rating fluctuates day by day across your tracked locations. Reading the Chart: The left axis measures the average rating (from 0.0 to 5.0 ), and the bottom axis displays the dates. The shaded blue area represents your daily average, making it easy to identify peaks (good days) and dips (bad days). Time Range Filter: Use the dropdown menu located at the top right of this specific section to adjust the chart's timeframe. You can toggle between viewing data for the Last 24 hours , Last 7 days , or Last 30 days . 4. Aggregate Topics Word Cloud The Aggregate Topics section features a word cloud that extracts the most common themes and keywords mentioned by your reviewers. The visual size of a word reflects its frequency; the larger and bolder the text appears, the more often customers brought that specific topic up in their written feedback.

label: Matched Influencers
description: Learn how to review your matched influencers, track their content, analyze risk assessments, and view posts about your brand.
content: Matched Influencers The Matched Influencers tab displays all the creators from the general influencer pool that have been checked and matched against your company. Here, you can evaluate their brand fit, track their ongoing content, review detailed performance benchmarks, and see posts they have created about your brand. 1. Accessing Your Matched List 1. Navigate to the Influencers page using the main sidebar. 2. Click on the Matched Influencers tab 3. Each matched influencer card displays a high level summary along with two primary actions: Details: Opens a dedicated, multi tabbed analytics dashboard for that creator. Posts About Me: Displays all tracked posts created by that influencer that specifically mention or relate to your company. Note: If your matched list is empty, you probably haven't checked or matched any influencers yet. Learn how to match influencers here. 2. Profile Overview & Quick Actions Clicking the Details button opens the creator's full profile page. The top header section includes several key controls: Social Profile Links: Quick links to open the influencer's official social media profiles (e.g., TikTok). Start Tracking (Eye Icon): Click the Start Tracking button to begin actively monitoring the creator. Once enabled, dima will automatically fetch and index their new posts moving forward. Full Bio: Click Show More to expand and read the creator's complete channel biography. Brand Relevance Score: A circular progress bar representing how closely the creator's content and audience align with your company parameters. 3. Deep Dive Profile Tabs From the influencer details page, you can navigate through four main analysis tabs: Content View the creator's major posts broken down by performance and topic. This includes their highest performing posts , lowest performing posts , and top content grouped by industry category (e.g., Lifestyle , Entertainment & Pop Culture ). Risk Assessment The Risk Assessment tab flags public incidents, legal issues, or controversies associated with the influencer that could impact your brand reputation: Plain Language Summaries: Clear explanations detailing what happened and what role the influencer played in the event (e.g., whether they were the responsible party , the affected party , or resolved the issue ). Source Citation Links: Bracketed numbers (e.g., [1]) link directly to the news articles or official reports where the information originated. Post Insights Review detailed charts analyzing creator engagement across various content categories: Engagement Rate by Followers: Measures audience interactions (likes, comments, shares) relative to their total follower count. Engagement Rate by Views: Measures interactions against actual view counts to show true audience engagement per post. Average Engagement Per Category: Bar charts displaying the average volume of interactions across different content subjects. Hover over any bar to view the exact interaction numbers.

label: Influencers Pool
description: Learn how to review an influencer's performance, assess risks, and match them with your brand.
content: Evaluating & Matching Influencers dima allows you to search for influencers, dive deep into their analytics, and check if they are a relevant match for your brand. This evaluation process takes place entirely within the Influencers Pool tab. 1. Accessing Influencer Profiles 1. Navigate to the Influencers page using the main sidebar. 2. Open the Influencers Pool tab to browse the available profiles. 3. Click on any influencer's card to open their detailed profile panel. 4. To browse more profiles, scroll down and use the Next pagination button located at the bottom center of the page. 2. Reviewing Influencer Analytics Once you open a profile, a detailed panel will appear with in depth statistics. Use the scrollbar within this panel to explore the different sections: Performance Intelligence & Benchmarks: Review the influencer's overall views, engagement rates, and how they stack up against industry standards. Risk Assessment: Identify potential red flags or controversies before engaging with the influencer. Audience Interest Mapping: Understand the demographics and core topics that resonate most with their followers. Community Resonance & Stability Floor: Click these metrics to view the exact posts that generated the influencer's highest (Resonance) and lowest (Stability Floor) engagement. Pro Tip (Exporting Data): You can easily export this profile data by clicking the Download Report button located at the top right corner of the details panel. 3. Checking Brand Relevance (Matching) After reviewing the analytics, you can run a targeted check to see how well the influencer aligns with your specific brand and topics. Scroll to the very bottom of the Influencer Details section and click the Check Brand Relevance button. Alternatively , you can click the quick Match icon directly on their profile header. dima will then analyze their historical content and audience against your specific brand parameters to determine their compatibility.

label: Influencer Impact Analytics
description: Learn how to analyze influencer performance, compare platforms, and filter impact data.
content: Influencer Impact Analytics The Influencer Impact Analytics page provides a comprehensive overview and detailed visual charts regarding your influencers' performance. 1. Viewing and Understanding Your Impact Analytics To access performance analytics, simply click the Influencer Impact Analytics tab within the Influencers page in the sidebar. This opens a comprehensive dashboard displaying a variety of charts and tables that help you interpret your influencers' results. The Overview Table At the top of the page, the Influencers Overview table lists each influencer along with their platform, views, engagement, and total post count. Pie Charts (Who is working) The pie charts tell you which specific influencer is performing best. A larger slice represents a higher number. Post Count by Influencer: Shows who posts the most. Engagement by Influencer: Shows who gets the most likes, comments, and shares. Views by Influencer: Shows who gets seen the most. Tip: You can use the two icons in the top right corner of any pie chart to switch between a piechart view and a barchart view. Bar Charts (Which platform is working) The bar charts show you which social platform is performing best, so you know where to focus your efforts. The colors inside each bar represent different influencers posting on that platform. Post Count by Platform: Shows how many posts went out on platforms like YouTube, Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram. Engagement by Platform: Shows which platform gets the most reactions. Views by Platform: Shows which platform generates the most views. Tip: Use the Display Top 10 button in the top right corner of these charts to limit the view to your ten biggest performers. 2. Using the Impact Filter To narrow down the data shown in your dashboard, click the Filter button in the top right corner of the page. The filter panel is divided into two main tabs on its left edge: General and Content . The General Tab Sentiment: Filter content by Positive, Negative, or Neutral sentiment tiles. Emotion: Filter by specific feelings, including Trust, Joy, Fear, Surprise, Sadness, Disgust, Anger, and Anticipation. Platform: Select one or multiple platforms, including X, Facebook, Web, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and Snapchat. The Content Tab Influencers: Click the "Select influencers..." dropdown to search and tick specific profiles, or use "Select All". Topic: Click the "Select topics..." dropdown to filter by specific subjects (e.g., General, Smartphones, Laptops). Label: Click the "Select labels..." dropdown to filter by your custom tags. Type: Use the 2x2 grid at the bottom to select one or multiple post types, including Organic Mentions, Public Groups, Private Groups, and Own Page. Applying Your Filters Once you have made your selections, click the Apply button in the bottom right corner of the panel to update your dashboard. (Note: You can click the Reset button to clear your choices, or click the X in the top right corner to close the panel without applying changes.)

label: Filtering Influencers
description: Learn how to narrow down your influencer pool by size, region, category, and platform to find the perfect match.
content: Filtering Influencers When searching for the right personalities to represent your brand, dima allows you to filter through the influencer pool using specific criteria. You can easily filter influencers by their audience size, geographic region, content categories, and the platforms they are active on. 1. Accessing the Filter Menu 1. Navigate to the Influencers page using the main sidebar. 2. Once in the Influencers module (whether you are looking at the general pool or your matched lists), click the Filter button located at the top right corner of the page. 2. Configuring Your Search Criteria The filter menu provides several categories to help you narrow down your search. You can select one or multiple options within each of the following sections: Influencer Size: Choose the tier of influencer you are looking for based on their following (e.g., Nano, Micro, Macro, Mega). Click on your desired options to select them. Region: Use this dropdown menu to target influencers based in specific locations. You can type in the textbox to quickly search for a region, or click to select from the list. Categories: Narrow down influencers by the topics they cover (e.g., Tech, Fashion, Food). Just like the Region field, you can type to search or click to select your desired categories from the dropdown. Platform: Select the specific social media channels you want the influencer to be active on (e.g., Instagram, YouTube, TikTok) by clicking the corresponding platform icons. 3. Applying the Filter Once you have configured all your desired criteria across the different sections, click the Apply button located at the bottom right corner of the menu. Your influencer list will instantly update to show only the profiles that match your specific requirements.

label: Monitoring Product Reviews
description: Learn how to track and analyze customer feedback for your products across major e-commerce platforms.
content: Monitoring Product Reviews The E Commerce Reviews page allows you to track customer feedback for your company's products across major e commerce websites. dima automatically aggregates reviews from platforms like Amazon, Noon, Jarir, Nahdi, and Extra into a single, unified feed. 1. Navigating the Reviews Feed When you open the Reviews tab, you will see a chronological list of customer feedback. Each review card provides a comprehensive snapshot of the interaction and the product it belongs to: Product Information: The product's name, thumbnail image, and its overall average star rating on the platform. E commerce Platform: The specific website where the review was posted (e.g., Amazon, Noon). Reviewer Details: The name of the customer who left the review. Review Content: The specific star rating given by the reviewer, the exact text of their review, and the date it was posted. Quick Link: Clicking directly on the product's name will instantly redirect you to the live e commerce listing for that product in a new tab. 2. Viewing Related Reviews If you want to dive deeper into a specific product's feedback without leaving the platform: 1. Click anywhere on a specific review card from your main feed. 2. A detailed panel will slide out from the right side of your screen. 3. This panel displays the full details of the review you clicked, while also aggregating other reviews for that exact same product . This allows you to quickly gauge overall customer sentiment and identify recurring themes for a specific item in one place.

label: Generating Reviews Insights
description: Learn how to use AI-driven insights to ask questions and summarize feedback from your e-commerce product reviews.
content: Product Reviews Insights The Insights tab within the E Commerce Reviews page allows you to ask specific, custom questions about your product reviews and receive AI generated summaries based on real customer feedback. 1. Generating Custom Insights Instead of reading through hundreds of individual reviews, you can ask dima to do the heavy lifting for you: 1. Navigate to the Insights Tab: Within the E Commerce Reviews page, click on the Insights tab located at the top of the page (next to Reviews and Analytics). 2. Enter Your Inquiry: In the Inquiry text box, type your specific question or prompt. For example, you can ask dima to "Summarize the most common complaints about product quality." 3. Generate: Click the blue Generate Insights button located just below the text field on the right side. 2. Reviewing Results and Sources Once dima processes your request, the AI generated analysis will appear in the Result box below. Comprehensive Summary: The result will provide a detailed, easy to read answer based directly on the collected feedback from your customers. Source Citations: Throughout the generated text, you will notice small bracketed numbers (e.g., [4], [12]). These are direct source links to the referring URLs. You can click on these numbers to trace the AI's claims back to the exact customer reviews that were used to generate the response, ensuring complete transparency and verifiability.

label: Using Filters
description: Learn how to narrow down your e-commerce reviews data by platform, review rating, and product rating.
content: Filtering E Commerce Reviews To help you zero in on specific feedback, the E Commerce Reviews page includes a dedicated Filters menu. These filters are persistent, meaning any criteria you select will apply seamlessly across all three tabs: Reviews , Analytics , and Insights . 1. Filter Categories When you open the Filters menu, you can narrow down your data using the following criteria: Platform: Select one or multiple specific e commerce storefronts to view data exclusively from those sources. Available platforms include Amazon, Noon, Nahdi, Jarir, and Extra. Review Rating: Filter the feed based on the specific star rating a customer left on their individual review (from 1 to 5 stars). Product Rating: Filter the feed based on the overall, cumulative average star rating of the products being reviewed. 2. Applying Your Filters Check the boxes next to the criteria you want to use. Click the blue Apply button at the bottom right of the menu to update your dashboard and feed. If you want to clear your current selections and start over, click the Reset button next to Apply.

label: Analytics Dashboard
description: Learn how to interpret the analytics dashboard to track product sentiment, ratings, and review volume over time.
content: Product Reviews Analytics To help you identify broader trends in customer feedback, the E Commerce Reviews page includes a dedicated analytics dashboard. This page visualizes your aggregate review data across all connected platforms, making it easy to spot performance spikes, drops in sentiment, or your most talked about products. 1. Sentiment & Volume (Over Time) These charts help you track how often customers are reviewing your products and how they feel, broken down by either days or weeks. Daily & Weekly Sentiment & Volume: These are combination charts. The stacked bar charts display the sentiment distribution (Positive, Neutral, Negative) of the reviews received during that specific day or week. The blue line graph layered over the bars tracks the total volume of reviews published in that same timeframe. 2. Ratings & Platform Breakdown Understand your overall product scores and find out where your customers are the most vocal. Weekly Average Rating: This chart tracks your overall average star rating on a week by week basis, allowing you to easily spot if product satisfaction is trending upwards or downwards over time. Reviews by Platform: A straightforward chart that counts the total number of reviews aggregated from each specific e commerce website (e.g., Amazon, Noon, Jarir). This helps you determine which storefront generates the most customer engagement. 3. Top Performing Products This bar chart highlights the products that are generating the most buzz and feedback. Review Volume & Star Breakdown: The overall height of each bar represents the total number of reviews a specific product has received. Stacked Star Ratings: Each bar is further divided into color coded segments that represent the exact breakdown of 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 star ratings making up that total volume. This makes it instantly clear whether a highly reviewed product is popular for good or bad reasons. 4. The Review Word Cloud The Word Cloud extracts the most frequently used terms from your customers' written reviews. The larger the word appears, the more often it was mentioned. View Toggles: You can switch the word cloud from a Normal view (neutral coloring) to a Sentiment view. Sentiment Coloring: When the sentiment view is activated, every word in the cloud is automatically color coded to reflect its context: Green (Positive), Orange (Neutral), or Red (Negative).

label: Monitoring Comments
description: Learn how to track and analyze comments and replies to understand community sentiment beyond the top-level post.
content: Monitoring Comments While tracking top level posts is crucial, true audience intelligence often lies in the comment section. dima's Conversation Analysis module allows you to dive deep into comment threads and replies to analyze how the community is actually reacting. 1. Accessing and Navigating Comments To get started, navigate to your main sidebar and click on the Conversation Analytics tab. This will open a dedicated feed displaying tracked posts alongside their top level comments and replies. When browsing the Conversation Analysis feed, you will see a preview of the comments attached to each post: To see more replies: Use the pagination controls located below the visible replies to navigate through the rest of the comment thread. To inspect a specific interaction: Simply click anywhere on a comment or reply card . This will open a detailed information panel. 2. The Detailed View Clicking on a comment opens a comprehensive view that gives you the full context of that specific interaction, including its origin and AI driven insights. The detailed view panel includes: Platform Origin: An icon at the top (e.g., Instagram, Twitter) showing exactly where the conversation is taking place. Original Post Context: The full caption of the original parent post, along with its direct URL. Engagement Metrics: The current performance of the parent post, including likes, comments, shares, views, and saves. Top Replies: The specific comment threads branching off the interaction. AI Insights: dima's automated analysis for the specific comment, displaying its Topic , Sentiment , and Emotion .

label: Using Filters
description: Learn how to filter comment threads based on both the original post's attributes and the specific attributes of the replies.
content: Using Filters Because the Conversation Analysis module focuses on threads and comments, it features a specialized filtering system. Unlike standard filters, this system allows you to cross reference data; meaning you can filter based on the attributes of the original post and the attributes of the replies underneath it (e.g., finding a post with a "Positive" sentiment that generated "Negative" replies). 1. Accessing the Filter 1. Navigate to the Conversation Analytics tab using the main sidebar. 2. Click the Filters button located at the top right corner of the page (just below the company logo). 2. Configuring the Filter Categories The Conversation Analysis filter menu is divided into two main sections: General and Content . You can select one or multiple options across both tabs. The General Tab This tab focuses on the mood and origin of the interaction. You can filter by: Post Sentiment & Emotion: The overall mood of the original top level post. Reply Sentiment & Emotion: The mood of the specific comments reacting to the post. Post Type: The nature of the post (e.g., Public, Owned). The Content Tab This tab focuses on the categorization of the text itself. You can filter by: Post Topics & Labels: The subjects and custom tags assigned to the original post. Reply Topics: The subjects being discussed within the comment section itself. 3. Dynamic Post Type Rules When configuring your filters, pay special attention to the Post Types category, as it behaves dynamically based on your selections: Important Note: If you select Public Group or Private Group as your only Post Type option, dima will automatically prompt you to enter the specific Facebook Group link you want to filter by. Similarly, if you select Own Page as your only option, you will be prompted to select which specific connected page you want to view. 4. Applying the Filter Once you have configured your desired criteria across the General and Content tabs, click the Apply Filters button located at the bottom right corner of the menu to update your conversation feed.

label: Analytics Dashboard
description: Learn how to analyze the sentiment, emotion, and topics of comments and replies on your official pages.
content: Analytics Dashboard The Conversation Analysis module includes a dedicated Analytics dashboard that focuses entirely on the comment sections of your official pages. Here, you can analyze the sentiment, emotion, and volume of community replies over a given period. 1. Accessing the Analytics Dashboard 1. Navigate to the Conversation Analytics tab using the main sidebar. 2. Click on the Analytics tab located at the top right of the page, just below the Filters button. 2. Reply Sentiment and Emotion (Over Time) These charts track the mood of your audience's replies on a day by day basis. Stacked Percentage Bars: Each vertical bar represents one day and is split into colored segments that always add up to 100% . For example, the Sentiment bar is made of green (Positive), red (Negative), and orange (Neutral). The left Y axis ( 0–100% ) measures these percentages. Total Volume Line: The blue line tracks the actual number of replies that day, completely separate from the percentages. It is measured by the right Y axis. Volume vs. Engagement Toggle: Use the top right toggle button to switch what the blue line represents (raw reply volume vs. total engagement). Interactive Breakdown: Hover over any bar to see the exact numerical breakdown for that specific day. AI Integration: dima can provide deeper insights on any graph. Simply hover over the graph you want to analyze and click the Add to chat icon that appears in the corner to add it to dima for further exploration. 3. The Reply Word Cloud & Stop Words The Reply Word Cloud displays the words or hashtags that appear most often in your comment sections. Larger, bolder text means the word is mentioned more frequently. Words vs. Hashtags: Use the top left toggle to switch between analyzing everyday words or specific hashtags. Color Coding: Use the top right buttons to change the coloring: Normal: A neutral, standard color scheme. Sentiment / Emotion: Colors each word based on whether it is associated with a positive/negative reaction or a specific emotional tone. Filtering Out Stop Words If you want to exclude common or unwanted words (like "the" or "and") from your Word Cloud, you can use the Stop Words feature: 1. Click the Stop Words button at the top right of the Reply Word Cloud section. 2. Click Add Stop Word . 3. Type the exact word you want dima to ignore into the text box. 4. Click Add to save it, then click the X to close the pop up. 4. Reply Distribution by Topic The Reply Sentiment/Emotion per Topic charts allow you to filter your analysis down to a single subject to see how people feel about specific aspects of your business. Topic Selection: Use the dropdown at the top left (e.g., "Smartphones" or "Consumer Financing") to filter the chart. It will update to show the sentiment or emotion only for replies related to that specific topic. Actual Counts: Each slice of the pie shows a specific category, and the number inside the slice represents the actual count of replies, not a percentage. View Toggles: Use the icons in the top right corner to switch seamlessly between a Pie chart view and a Bar/Column chart view. 5. Overall Reply Distribution These charts give you the big picture of your comment sections at a glance, without breaking it down day by day. Reply Sentiment Distribution: Sorts all replies into Positive, Negative, and Neutral groups to show the overall reaction. Reply Emotion Distribution: Breaks the same replies down into specific granular emotions (e.g., Joy, Trust, Anticipation, Surprise, Sadness, Anger, Disgust, and Fear) so you can see exactly what people were feeling. Chart Views: Like the Topic charts, these display actual reply counts rather than percentages, and you can toggle between Pie and Bar views using the icons in the top right corner. The legend below each chart lists every category with its color and count for easy reference.

label: Using Filters
description: Learn how to filter your social and media data by sentiment, demographics, topics, and platforms.
content: Filtering Data When viewing data in the Own Page , Groups , or Audience Intelligence modules, dima provides a powerful filtering system to help you narrow down your posts. You can filter data using a variety of factors, including sentiment, emotion, topic, platform, language, and demographics. 1. Using the Filter Modal To access the standard filters, click the Filter button located at the top right corner of the page. This opens a modal divided into four tabs: Sentiment & Emotion: Select one or more options to view posts with specific positive/negative sentiments or emotional tones. Topics & Labels: Type or select specific Topics and Labels from the dropdown menus to find categorized posts. Platforms & Post Type: Filter posts by their origin platform (e.g., Twitter, Facebook). Demographic: Narrow down the audience by selecting one or more Languages, Regions, or Genders. Note on Dynamic Filters: The available fields in the Platforms tab will change depending on which page you are currently viewing. If you are on the Own Pages tab, you can select specific Own Pages. If you are on the Groups tab, you can enter specific Facebook Group links. Once you have configured your desired criteria across any of the tabs, click the Apply button at the bottom right of the menu. 2. Using the In Page Expanded View If you prefer to see all your filtering options at a glance without clicking through a tabbed modal, dima offers an expanded in page view. 1. Look for the expand icon located between the Filter and Download Report buttons at the top right corner of the page. 2. Click this icon to toggle the Expanded Filter view. 3. Instead of opening a popup, all the filtering criteria mentioned above will render directly on the page as accessible button toggles.

label: Using The Date Filter
description: Learn how to filter your analytics and dashboard data by specific date ranges across various modules.
content: Using The Date Filter Whenever you open an analytics page in dima, it loads with a default date range applied. The Date Filter allows you to adjust this range to find specific posts, influencers, reviews, and chart data for a given timeframe. This filter is available across most modules, including: Audience Intelligence (Monitor, Analysis, Users, Topic Insights) Groups Own Page Made For You (When opening an already created dashboard) Conversation Analysis Influencers Locations E Commerce Review Manage (Deleted Posts) 1. Opening The Date Picker To change the timeframe of the data you are viewing, click the date range button located at the top of the page. This button always displays the currently applied range (e.g., "Jul 09, 2026 Aug 09, 2026"). Clicking it will open the date picker menu, which offers several ways to select a new range. 2. Selecting a Date Range You can choose your new date range using any of the following four methods: Quick Ranges The left column of the date picker contains ready made ranges for fast filtering: Today / Yesterday: Snaps the data to a single specific day. Last 7 / 14 days: Shows a rolling window of recent performance. This month / Last month: Sets the range to the exact calendar month (e.g., from the 1st up to today). Week of the Year If you want to view a specific numbered week, click Week of year in the left column. Two dropdowns will appear below the column, allowing you to explicitly select the Year and the Week Number (e.g., Year: 2026, Week: 30). Calendar Selection For a custom free form range, interact directly with the two month calendar in the center of the picker. 1. Click your desired start day . 2. Click your desired end day . 3. The calendar will highlight the entire period between the two dates. (You can click a new date at any time to restart the selection). Manual Date Entry If you prefer to type the exact dates, use the input boxes located at the bottom of the date picker. You can directly enter the Month, Day, and Year for both the start and end dates. 3. Applying the Filter Once you are satisfied with your selected range, click the Set Date button at the bottom right of the picker. The page will immediately reload, and all charts and lists will filter to match your new timeframe. Note: If you change your mind, you can click Cancel next to the Set Date button to close the picker without applying any changes.

label: Analytics Dashboards
description: Understand the charts and metrics available in the Analytics tab across different modules to track performance, sentiment, and distribution.
content: Understanding Analytics Dashboards The Analytics tab in dima provides a suite of visualizations to help you understand your data's performance, sentiment, and audience distribution. These charts are available in the Own Page , Groups , and Audience Intelligence modules. Below is a breakdown of every chart you will find in the Analytics view and how to interpret them. 1. Timing and Progression These charts help you identify when to post and how your overall performance is trending over time. Aggregated Top Posts per Hour: This 24 hour circular clock shows what time of day your best performing posts go out. The further a spike stretches from the center, the more top posts happened at that hour (e.g., long spikes at 18:00 and 21:00 indicate evening is your strongest window). Top Posts per Day of Week: A bar chart showing which days of the week generate your best posts. A taller bar means more strong posts on that day. Average Progression: A line chart tracking your page's average performance over time. A climbing line indicates growth, while a steady flat line means performance is stable. Individual Progression: Similar to Average Progression, but it plots a separate colored line for each account or page you are tracking, allowing for direct comparison. 2. Volume and Engagement Top Engagement Volume Chart: This chart combines two metrics. The shaded blue line shows your daily posting volume, while the floating bubbles represent top posts. A bubble's height indicates the time of day it was posted, and a bigger bubble means higher performance. Controls: Use the top right buttons to switch the chart's focus between Volume (amount posted), Engagement (amount of reaction), and Engagement Sentiment (colors bubbles by positive/neutral/negative reactions). 3. Sentiment and Emotion These charts break down the mood and feelings surrounding your posts. Post Sentiment Distribution (Over Time): Shows how the mood of your posts changed day by day. Each bar represents a date and is split by percentage into Positive, Neutral, and Negative. The blue line across the chart indicates your total volume for that day. Post Emotion Distribution (Over Time): The same layout as Sentiment Distribution, but broken down into specific granular emotions. Sentiment & Emotion Distribution (Aggregated): Pie charts that provide the overall mood of all your posts for the selected period. The numbers inside each slice represent the actual count of posts. Use the top right icons to toggle between a Pie view and a Bar view. Sentiment & Emotion by Topic: Narrows down the mood to a single subject. Use the dropdown menu at the top left to select a specific topic (e.g., Customer Service) and see the mood for only the posts about that subject. Sentiment & Emotion by Platform: Compares the mood of your content across different platforms (e.g., Facebook, TikTok, LinkedIn) side by side. Because it is shown as a percentage, you are comparing the mix of sentiment on each platform, not the volume. The blue line represents the total volume of posts to provide context. 4. Audience and Platform Distribution These charts tell you where your posts are being seen and who is interacting with them. Country Distribution: A pie chart showing where your posts or audience are coming from by country, displaying actual counts. Language Distribution: A pie chart breaking down the audience by language (e.g., Arabic vs. English). Volume Distribution by Platform: Shows where you are posting the most content (number of posts per platform). Views Distribution by Platform: Shows which social platform is actually delivering the most views. Comparing this to Volume Distribution reveals if you are posting heavily on a platform that isn't returning views. Engagement Distribution by Platform: Shows which platform generates the most reactions (likes, comments, shares). 5. The Word Cloud Word Cloud: Displays the words that appear most frequently across your posts. The larger the word, the more often it was used. Controls: Use the left tabs to switch between normal Words and Hashtags. Use the right buttons to color the words based on Sentiment or Emotion. The Stop Words toggle allows you to hide common filler words (like "the" or "and").

label: Sorting Posts
description: Learn how to arrange posts in your monitoring feed based on metrics such as likes, comments, views, or follower count.
content: Sorting Posts When reviewing large amounts of data in your monitoring feeds, you may want to prioritize certain posts. dima allows you to dynamically sort your feed by key metrics including date, likes, comments, shares, and views. How to Sort Your Feed 1. Open the Sort Menu: While on any monitoring page (such as Audience Intelligence, Groups, or Own Page), locate and click the Sort icon above the posts feed. 2. Choose Sorting Factors: A menu will appear listing the available metrics. Click on the factor(s) you want to use to sort your posts. You can select more than one factor if you want to establish primary and secondary sorting rules. 3. Set the Order (Ascending/Descending): Once a factor is selected, an arrow icon will appear to its right. Click this icon to toggle the sorting direction: Descending (Arrow Down): Shows the highest numbers first (e.g., most likes to least likes). Ascending (Arrow Up): Shows the lowest numbers first (e.g., fewest views to most views). 4. Apply Your Sort: After configuring your desired factors and order, click the Apply Sort button at the bottom of the pop up menu. Your feed will immediately reload in the new arrangement.

label: Pinning Posts
description: Learn how to pin specific posts to the top of your monitoring feed for easy tracking and crisis management.
content: Pinning Posts When you are tracking a viral trend, handling a PR crisis, or simply keeping a close eye on a specific conversation, you can pin posts to ensure they are always highly visible. Pinning a post anchors it to the very top of your monitoring page, completely overriding any sorting methods you have applied (such as sorting by views or engagement). How to Pin a Post 1. Navigate to the Audience Intelligence module using the main sidebar. 2. Open the Monitor tab to view your feed of tracked posts. 3. Locate the specific post you want to track. 4. Click the Star icon located in the bottom right corner of the post card. The post is now pinned and will immediately move to the very top of your feed. Important Note on Filters: While pinned posts ignore sorting rules, they still obey filtering rules. If you apply a filter (such as a specific date range, sentiment, or platform) that the pinned post does not match, it will temporarily disappear from your feed until you clear the filter.

label: Generating & Downloading Reports
description: Learn how to select posts, add them to a collection, and export them as presentations, tables, or emails.
content: Generating & Downloading Reports dima allows you to handpick specific posts and compile them into a customized report for analytical purposes. You can export these reports in several formats including Table, Presentation, and Email which you can send them directly to your contacts. This reporting feature is available across the Audience Intelligence , Groups , and Own Page modules. 1. Adding Posts to Your Report Collection Before you can download or send a report, you first need to select the posts you want to include. 1. Select Individual Posts: Hover over the post you want to include, then click the checkbox that appears at the top right corner. 2. Select All Posts (Optional): To bulk select, use the Select All icon (or its neighboring dropdown) located above the posts feed. 3. Add to Collection: Once your posts are selected, click the Add selected to Report icon (the download arrow icon located between the posts' statistics and the posts themselves). 2. Reviewing and Formatting the Report Once you have added posts to your collection, you can review them and choose your export format. 1. Click the Download Report button located at the top right corner of the page (just below the company logo). 2. A pop up will appear displaying all the posts currently in your report collection. 3. Refine your list: If you need to remove a post from the report, hover over it and click the Trash icon next to the post's URL. You can also click Clear All at the bottom left to empty the entire collection. 4. Choose a Format: At the bottom right corner of the pop up, click on your desired report type (e.g., Table, Presentation, Email). Pro Tip (Quick Export): If you don't need to review your posts, you can skip the review pop up entirely by clicking the dropdown arrow directly next to the "Download Report" button and selecting your template from there. 3. Sending and Downloading After selecting your report format, a final Send confirmation pop up will appear. 1. Select Recipients: Use the Contacts dropdown to choose who should receive the report. You can type an email address in the search box to quickly find someone. Note: If you don't see any contacts available to select, you'll need to create them first. Learn how to add a contact here. 2. Manage Collection: By default, posts are removed from your collection after the report is sent. If you want to reuse this batch of posts for another report, check the "Keep posts in collection" box. 3. Finish: Click the Send button at the bottom right corner of the pop up to generate and distribute the report.

label: Deleting Posts & Recalibrating Relevancy
description: Learn how to remove irrelevant posts from your feed and train dima to improve future monitoring accuracy.
content: Deleting Posts & Recalibrating Relevancy Sometimes, dima might fetch a post that contains your tracked keywords but is completely unrelated to your actual brand or industry. You can easily delete these irrelevant posts from your feed. More importantly, dima allows you to recalibrate its AI based on your deletions, ensuring similar irrelevant posts stop showing up in the future. 1. Deleting Irrelevant Posts You can delete posts and trigger the AI recalibration process directly from the Monitor page. 1. Navigate to the Audience Intelligence module and open the Monitor tab. 2. Browse your feed and select the posts you want to remove by clicking the checkbox at the top right corner of each post card. 3. Once your posts are selected, click the Delete icon (the trash can) located in the toolbar above the posts feed. Pro Tip for AI Training: If you select at least 5 posts before deleting, dima will automatically prompt you to recalibrate its relevancy engine so it can learn from your cleanup. 2. Recalibrating dima's AI After removing posts, the Recalibrate Relevancy dialog will automatically open. This is where you tell dima exactly what it should ignore moving forward. (Note: You can also manually open this dialog at any time by clicking the Recalibrate relevancy icon (the target/bullseye) in the main toolbar. This toolbar is located between the stats area and the posts feed.) Providing Examples via URLs You can give dima direct examples of what not to track. Under the Irrelevant Posts column on the right, click Add Irrelevant Post . Paste the exact URL of the post you consider unrelated to your brand into the new link box. You can add multiple links. If you make a mistake, simply click the Trash icon next to the link to remove it. Providing Plain Text Instructions Instead of (or in addition to) providing links, you can give the AI direct, plain language instructions. Locate the Requested Relevancy Adjustment text box at the bottom of the dialog. Describe exactly what you want dima to filter out (e.g., "Ignore posts about Apple the fruit, I only want posts about Apple computers and laptops." ). 3. Submitting Your Request Once you have added your URLs or typed your instructions: 1. Click the Submit request button at the bottom right of the dialog. (If you do not want to train the AI right now, you can click Not now ). 2. A confirmation message will appear stating: "Request received! dima is learning from your feedback." 3. Click the X in the top right corner to close the window. Note: Please allow up to 24 hours for dima to fully process your feedback and adjust your data feed accordingly.

label: Bulk Actions
description: Learn how to perform collective actions on multiple posts, such as updating sentiment, changing topics, or assigning labels simultaneously.
content: Using Bulk Actions When managing a large volume of data in dima, you may want to apply the same change to several posts at once. The Bulk Actions feature allows you to simultaneously assign or remove labels, change sentiments and emotions, update topics, or even delete multiple posts. 1. Selecting Posts Before applying a bulk action, you first need to select the posts you wish to modify. 1. Navigate to the Audience Intelligence page (or any other module displaying a feed of posts). 2. Click the checkbox located in the top right corner of each post you want to include in your bulk update. 2. Using the Bulk Actions Menu Once at least one post is selected, a new set of action icons will appear above your feed. 1. Locate and click the Bulk Actions icon (represented by three vertical dots ⋮). 2. A menu will appear with tabs for the different attributes you can modify: Sentiment , Emotion , Topic , and Label . 3. Click through the tabs and select the new values you want to apply to your selected posts. 3. Creating and Assigning New Labels While in the Bulk Actions menu, you can easily apply existing labels or create brand new ones on the fly. To create or assign labels to your selected posts in bulk: A. Assigning Existing Labels In the Bulk Actions menu, go to the Label as tab. Click Assign Labels . Open the "Select Labels" dropdown and choose one or more labels from your company's list to apply them to all selected posts. B. Creating a New Label In the same "Select Labels" dropdown, click the + (Plus) icon to the right. An "Add Label" pop up will appear. Enter your desired label name in the Name textbox. Click the Add button at the bottom right to create the label. Your new label now appears in the dropdown and can be immediately selected and assigned. This organized menu lets you quickly apply any combination of new and existing labels during the bulk action process. 4. Applying Your Changes Once you have configured all your desired changes across the Sentiment, Emotion, Topic, or Label tabs, click the Apply button located at the bottom right of the page. dima will instantly process the update and apply your chosen criteria to all selected posts.

label: Switching Brands
description: Learn how to quickly switch your active workspace to view data and reports for a different company.
content: Switching Between Brands If you are monitoring multiple companies, dima allows you to easily jump between them without leaving your current page. Changing your active brand updates your dashboard, reports, and settings to reflect the selected company's data. How to Switch Your Active Brand You can switch brands from anywhere in the app using the main navigation sidebar. 1. Open the Switcher: Locate and click your current company's icon at the very bottom left corner of the sidebar. 2. Select a Brand: A menu will appear showing all the companies you have access to. Click the desired brand from the list to switch immediately. 3. Search (Optional): If you manage a large number of brands, type the company's name into the search bar at the top of the menu to find it quickly.

label: Adding a Company
description: Learn how to define a brand or subject matter in dima to start monitoring social media posts.
content: Adding a Company A Company in dima represents the brand, competitor, or subject matter you want to monitor (e.g., Tesla or Automotive Industry in Saudi Arabia ). Adding a company allows you to define tracking parameters like official page links, topics of interest, and Google Map locations. Once set up, dima will track relevant social media posts, allowing you to generate reports, receive alerts, and discover key insights. To get started, click the Add New Company button located at the first position on the Brands Page. Step 1: Company Details In this first step, you will provide the foundational information about the brand. 1. Company Name: Enter the official name of the company. 2. Company Description: Describe the company's products, services, market focus, and regions served. Note: This heavily helps dima understand what content is actually relevant to the brand. 3. Company Logo: Click the logo box on the right to upload a recognizable image (JPEG, max 5MB). 4. Currency & Country Code: Use the dropdowns at the bottom left to set the primary currency and operating country. 5. Competitors (Optional): If this company is a competitor to your main brand, check the "Is Competitor" box and select the primary company it competes with from the dropdown menu. Once filled out, click Next at the bottom right corner to move to Online Presence. Step 2: Online Presence (Optional) Note: Step 2 is completely optional . You may skip this for now. You can learn how to manage your company's online presence and links here at any time. This step tells dima exactly where to look for official posts, reviews, and targeted conversations. Post Topics Categorize and track specific types of mentions (e.g., tracking complaints vs. product praise). Click Add Topic . Give your topic a Name and a brief Description of what it covers (e.g., "Any feedback or complaints regarding customer service" ). Note: The "General" topic is a default and cannot be removed. It serves as a catch all for mentions that don't fit into your custom topics. Own Page Links Link the brand's official social media profiles so dima can distinguish between the brand's own posts and public mentions. 1. Click Add Own Page . 2. Enter a Name for the page and select the Platform (e.g., Twitter, LinkedIn) from the dropdown. 3. Paste the exact URL of the profile. 4. Tracking Scope: By default, dima tracks all posts from the last 30 days. If you want to limit tracking to specific types of posts, uncheck "Track all posts" and leave a comment specifying what dima should track. Google Map Links Link physical locations to monitor Google Reviews. 1. Click Add Location . 2. Give the location a Name (e.g., "Main Branch HQ" ). 3. Paste the exact Google Maps URL . Group Links Track conversations happening inside specific Facebook groups. 1. Click Add Group and provide a Name . 2. Paste the Facebook Group URL . 3. Tracking Scope: Just like Own Pages, you can choose to track all posts or specify rules (e.g., "Only track posts mentioning drinks" ) by unchecking the tracking box and leaving a comment. Click Next to move to Posts Relevancy. Step 3: Posts Relevancy (Optional) Note: Step 3 is also completely optional . You can learn more about defining posts relevancy criteria here if you want to refine what dima should track or ignore for your company. In this step, you can train dima's AI by providing examples of what you do and do not want to see. This can drastically improve the accuracy of your media monitoring, but it is not required to proceed. Relevant Posts (Left Column): Click Add Relevant Post and paste the URL of a post that is a perfect example of what you want dima to track. Irrelevant Posts (Right Column): Click Add Irrelevant Post and paste the URL of a post that dima should ignore (e.g., a post about a company with a similar name in a different industry). You can add multiple examples for both. Once you are satisfied, click Next . Step 4: Review & Submit 1. Review all the configurations you have set across the previous steps. 2. Click the Submit button to complete the process. Note: dima will immediately begin analyzing your configuration and fetching historical data. Please allow up to 24 hours for the initial learning phase and data population to complete.
